sentences.text: The name Philovenator literally translates to "love hunter".
This animal was a small, bird-like, and gracile member of the troodontid group of maniraptoran dinosaurs.
A distinctive process on the inner side of the lower thighbone was one of the distinguishing traits of Philovenator.
The only known fossil of Philovenator is a single left hindlimb discovered in 1988 by the China-Canada Dinosaur Project.
Its foot bone was twenty-five times longer than it was wide.
As a troodontid, Philovenator possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and likely had keen senses and advanced behavior.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Philovenator as an advanced troodontid closely related to Saurornithoides, Zanabazar, and Troodon.
Philovenator belongs to the subfamily Jinfengopteryginae.
The fossil record for Philovenator spans from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
